required_quotations.quote: s. 38(3) of the Trustee Act, and not s. 4 of the RPLA, applies to the respondent's equitable trust claims

definitions.ISSUE-01: Whether the adult child is a dependant and whether adequate provision has been made for her proper support; what the Act directs the court to consider; and whether moral as well as needs-based claims may be weighed in Ontario.
definitions.ISSUE-02: The time limits: the period governing the support application, the effect of the certificate having issued ten months ago and the estate having been distributed, the discretion that remains; and separately which limitation period governs the unjust enrichment and constructive trust claim 26 months after death.
definitions.ISSUE-03: Which non-estate assets are brought back into the net estate for support purposes and under which provision, and what independent claim lies to the insurance proceeds, the joint account or the farm.
definitions.ISSUE-04: The claims for nine years of care: unjust enrichment and the joint family venture, the measure of a money award, and proprietary estoppel over the farm.
definitions.ISSUE-05: The will challenge: the threshold for an order that the will be proved in solemn form, the effect of suspicious circumstances on the burden, and whether a court will look behind an unambiguous bequest because of the testator's alleged motive.
definitions.PROP-01: A 'dependant' under s. 57(1) of the Succession Law Reform Act is a spouse, parent, child or sibling of the deceased to whom the deceased was providing support, or was under a legal obligation to provide support, immediately before death; s. 58(1) allows the court to order adequate provision out of the estate where the deceased has not made adequate provision for the proper support of a dependant, and s. 58(4) fixes the date of the hearing as the date for assessing adequacy.
definitions.PROP-02: Section 61(1) bars a support application more than six months after the grant of letters probate or letters of administration; s. 61(2) allows the court, if it considers it proper, to permit an application at any time as to any portion of the estate remaining undistributed at the date of the application.
definitions.PROP-03: Section 72(1) deems the capital value of listed transactions to be part of the net estate for Part V purposes, including joint bank accounts payable to the survivor (s. 72(1)(c)), dispositions creating a joint tenancy (s. 72(1)(d)), amounts payable under a policy of insurance on the life of the deceased and owned by the deceased (s. 72(1)(f)), and beneficiary designations (s. 72(1)(g)).
definitions.PROP-04: In deciding whether adequate provision has been made, an Ontario court examines the claims of all dependants, whether based on need or on legal or moral and ethical obligations; moral considerations have a part to play under s. 58(1), though not necessarily the same weight as in British Columbia (Cummings v. Cummings paras 27 and 32).
definitions.PROP-05: The two-year limitation in s. 38(3) of the Trustee Act, not the ten-year period in s. 4 of the Real Property Limitations Act, governs an equitable trust claim against an estate; the period runs from the death, and a claim brought more than two years after death is statute-barred (Ingram v. Kulynych Estate paras 56, 66 and 67).
definitions.PROP-06: Section 38(2) of the Trustee Act permits an action against the executor or administrator for a wrong committed by the deceased, and s. 38(3) provides that an action under that section shall not be brought after two years from the death of the deceased.
definitions.PROP-07: Section 72(1)(f) claws back into the net estate any amount payable under a policy of insurance effected on the life of the deceased and owned by the deceased, and s. 72(7) preserves the rights of a creditor in a transaction with respect to which a creditor has rights, which is how a support recipient designated irrevocable beneficiary is ranked (Dagg v. Cameron Estate paras 1, 2 and 4).
definitions.PROP-08: Unjust enrichment requires enrichment, corresponding deprivation and the absence of a juristic reason; where a joint family venture links the parties' joint efforts to an accumulation of wealth the claim addresses a disproportionate share of jointly earned assets, and a monetary award need not be confined to quantum meruit but may be assessed on a value-survived basis (Kerr v. Baranow paras 30, 55 and 60).
definitions.PROP-09: The principled unjust enrichment framework governs; a constructive trust is imposed only where a personal remedy would be inadequate and the contribution is linked to the property, and then only to the extent of the proportionate contribution (Moore v. Sweet paras 37 and 91).
definitions.PROP-10: An interested person must meet a minimal evidentiary threshold before a court will order a testamentary instrument proved in solemn form (Neuberger v. York para 88).
definitions.PROP-11: Where suspicious circumstances are present the presumption of knowledge and approval is spent and the propounder reassumes the legal burden of proving knowledge and approval, and testamentary capacity where the circumstances relate to capacity, on the civil standard (Vout v. Hay para 27).
definitions.PROP-12: The presumption of resulting trust applies to gratuitous transfers, and the presumption of advancement does not apply to independent adult children, so a joint account opened with an adult transferee is presumed to be held in trust (Pecore paras 24 and 36).
definitions.PROP-13: Proprietary estoppel arises where a representation or assurance is made, the claimant reasonably relies on the expectation it creates, and suffers detriment such that it would be unjust for the representor to go back on her word (Cowper-Smith v. Morgan para 15).
definitions.PROP-14: A court will not scrutinize an unambiguous residual bequest that contains no discriminatory condition on public policy grounds using third-party extrinsic evidence of the testator's motive (Spence v. BMO Trust Company para 1).
definitions.CONCLUSION-01: The client is a dependant and has a strong claim that adequate provision was not made, and the court may weigh the moral obligation arising from nine years of unpaid care.
definitions.CONCLUSION-02: The support application is out of time under s. 61(1) and can now reach only the roughly $9,000 remaining undistributed, if the court exercises its s. 61(2) discretion; the unjust enrichment and constructive trust claim against the estate is statute-barred because more than two years have passed since the death.
definitions.CONCLUSION-03: A challenge to the will on the basis of the testator's alleged motive will not succeed; the viable challenge is knowledge and approval and capacity through suspicious circumstances, and it requires the minimal evidentiary threshold to be met first.
definitions.CLAIM-01: The two-year discoverability rule in the Limitations Act, 2002 governs a dependant's support application under the Succession Law Reform Act.
definitions.CLAIM-02: Section 61(2) allows the court to extend time as to the whole estate, including assets already distributed.
definitions.CLAIM-03: Assets passing outside the will by survivorship or beneficiary designation are beyond the reach of a dependant's support order.
definitions.CLAIM-04: An equitable trust claim against an estate is governed by the ten-year period in s. 4 of the Real Property Limitations Act.
definitions.CLAIM-05: A monetary award for unjust enrichment must be calculated on a quantum meruit basis.
